title: Hans Christian Oersted's Discovery & The Concept of Magnetic Field
tagline: The unity of electricity and magnetism, compass deflection, and vector nature of magnetic fields.
theoryHtml:
1. Oersted's Epochal Experiment (1820)

In 1820, Danish physicist Hans Christian Oersted accidentally observed that a small magnetic compass needle placed near a metallic conducting wire was deflected whenever an electric current was switched on in the wire. When the current was turned off, the compass returned to its normal north-south orientation. Reversing the direction of current deflected the needle in the exact opposite direction!

This monumental experiment established for the first time in scientific history that moving electric charges (electric current) generate a magnetic field in the surrounding space, forging the foundational branch of physics known as electromagnetism.

2. What is a Magnetic Field ($\vec{B}$)?

A magnetic field is the region of space surrounding a magnet or a current-carrying conductor in which its magnetic force can be detected by other magnets or moving charges.

  • It is a vector quantity possessing both magnitude and direction.
  • The direction of the magnetic field at any point is defined as the direction in which the north pole of a magnetic compass needle points when placed at that point.
  • The SI unit of magnetic field intensity (magnetic flux density) is the tesla (T), named in honour of Nikola Tesla ($1\text{ T} = 1\text{ N}\cdot\text{A}^{-1}\cdot\text{m}^{-1} = 10^4\text{ Gauss}$).
pointsToRemember: Hans Christian Oersted (1820) discovered that an electric current produces a magnetic field.
Magnetic field is a VECTOR quantity having both magnitude and direction.
The SI unit of magnetic field strength is the Tesla ($\text{T}$).
keyNotes: A magnetic compass is simply a miniature bar magnet pivoted on a sharp spindle, whose north-seeking pole points toward Earth's geographic north.

questions.question: Which scientist first discovered in 1820 that an electric current flowing through a metallic wire produces a magnetic field that deflects a nearby compass needle?
questions.answer: Hans Christian Oersted
questions.explanation: Hans Christian Oersted discovered electromagnetism in 1820 when he noticed a compass needle deflect near a current-carrying wire.

questions.question: A compass needle placed near a magnet behaves as a small:
questions.answer: Bar magnet
questions.explanation: A magnetic compass needle is a small pivoted permanent bar magnet whose ends align with magnetic field lines.

questions.question: Which hand rule is used to determine the direction of mechanical force (or motion) acting on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field?
questions.answer: Fleming's left-hand rule
questions.explanation: Fleming's left-hand rule determines motor force: Forefinger = Field, Middle finger = Current, Thumb = Force/Motion.

questions.question: The unit of magnetic field strength named the 'oersted' honors Hans Christian Oersted. In SI units, magnetic field is measured in:
questions.answer: Tesla (T, where 1 T = 1 N / (A m))
questions.explanation: The SI unit of magnetic field intensity B is the tesla (T). 1 T = 1 N A⁻¹ m⁻¹.

questions.question: Why does an electric current in a metallic wire produce a magnetic field, whereas stationary electrostatic charges produce ONLY an electric field?
options: Stationary charges have no electric field
Moving charges create a dynamic changing electric flux that generates a circulating magnetic field according to Maxwell-Ampère electrodynamics
Electrons are tiny magnets when moving
Metals become cold when current flows
questions.answer: Moving charges create a dynamic changing electric flux that generates a circulating magnetic field according to Maxwell-Ampère electrodynamics
questions.explanation: Special relativity and Maxwell's equations demonstrate that moving charge elements generate magnetic fields via Lorentz transformations of electrostatic Coulomb fields.

questions.question: Which Danish scientist first discovered in 1820 that an electric current produces a magnetic field?
questions.answer: Hans Christian Oersted
questions.explanation: Hans Christian Oersted discovered electromagnetism in 1820 by observing the deflection of a compass needle near a current-carrying wire.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of magnetic field intensity (magnetic flux density)?
questions.answer: Tesla (T)
questions.explanation: The SI unit of magnetic field strength is the tesla (T), named after Nikola Tesla.

questions.question: Is the magnetic field a scalar quantity or a vector quantity, and why?
options: Scalar, because it only has energy
Vector, because it possesses both magnitude and direction at every point in space
Dimensionless, because it has no units
questions.answer: Vector, because it possesses both magnitude and direction at every point in space
questions.explanation: Magnetic field is a vector quantity; its direction is defined by the orientation of the north pole of a compass needle.

questions.question: What is a magnetic compass needle essentially composed of?
options: A tiny permanent bar magnet freely pivoted at its centre of gravity
questions.answer: A tiny permanent bar magnet freely pivoted at its centre of gravity
questions.explanation: A compass needle is a small permanent magnet whose north-seeking tip aligns with ambient magnetic field lines.

questions.question: What happens to the deflection of a compass needle placed below a horizontal wire when the direction of electric current in the wire is REVERSED?
options: The needle deflects in the exact opposite direction
The needle spins continuously at 100 rpm
questions.answer: The needle deflects in the exact opposite direction
questions.explanation: Reversing current reverses the direction of the concentric circular magnetic field, reversing the needle's deflection.

title: Magnetic Field Lines: Properties, Field Patterns & Non-Intersection Rule
tagline: Continuous closed loops, relative density as field strength, and why two lines never cross.
theoryHtml:
1. What are Magnetic Field Lines?

Magnetic field lines are imaginary continuous lines drawn in a magnetic field along which an isolated imaginary north magnetic pole would move if free to do so. The tangent drawn to a magnetic field line at any point indicates the exact direction of the magnetic field vector ($\vec{B}$) at that point.

2. Fundamental Properties of Magnetic Field Lines

  1. Continuous Closed Loops:
    • Outside the magnet: Field lines emerge from the North pole ($N$) and enter the South pole ($S$).
    • Inside the magnet: Field lines travel from the South pole ($S$) back to the North pole ($N$).
    • Therefore, magnetic field lines form unbroken, continuous closed loops. (This contrasts with electrostatic field lines, which start on positive charges and end on negative charges).
  2. Relative Crowding (Degree of Closeness): The degree of closeness (crowding) of the field lines represents the relative strength of the magnetic field. Where lines are crowded (near the poles), the field is strong; where lines are widely spaced, the field is weak.
  3. The Non-Intersection Rule: No two magnetic field lines can ever intersect or cross each other! If two lines crossed at a point $P$, a compass needle placed at that point would have to point simultaneously in two different directions at the same time—which is physically impossible.
pointsToRemember: Outside a magnet, field lines run North to South; inside, they run South to North (forming continuous closed loops).
Crowding of field lines indicates magnetic field strength (strongest at poles).
No two magnetic field lines can ever intersect, because that would imply two distinct field directions at one point.
keyNotes: Magnetic field lines are continuous closed curves because isolated magnetic monopoles do not exist in nature; cutting a magnet always produces a pair of dipoles (N and S).

questions.question: Outside a bar magnet, magnetic field lines emerge from the __________ pole and merge/enter at the __________ pole.
questions.answer: North; South
questions.explanation: By universal scientific convention, external magnetic field lines emerge from the North pole and enter the South pole.

questions.question: Inside the body of a bar magnet, what is the direction of magnetic field lines?
options: From North pole to South pole
From South pole to North pole (forming closed continuous loops)
There are no field lines inside a magnet
questions.answer: From South pole to North pole (forming closed continuous loops)
questions.explanation: Inside the magnet, field lines run from South to North, making magnetic field lines continuous closed curves.

questions.question: In Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, what do the Forefinger, Middle finger, and Thumb represent, respectively?
options: Forefinger: Current; Middle finger: Force; Thumb: Field
Forefinger: Magnetic Field; Middle finger: Electric Current; Thumb: Force / Motion
Forefinger: Force; Middle finger: Field; Thumb: Current
Forefinger: Voltage; Middle finger: Resistance; Thumb: Power
questions.answer: Forefinger: Magnetic Field; Middle finger: Electric Current; Thumb: Force / Motion
questions.explanation: Forefinger points in Magnetic Field (B), Middle finger in Current (I), and outstretched Thumb indicates Direction of Force (F).

questions.question: Imagine you are sitting in a chamber with your back to one wall. An electron beam traveling horizontally from the back wall towards the front wall is deflected strongly to your RIGHT by a magnetic field. What is the direction of the magnetic field?
questions.answer: Vertically downwards (towards the floor)
questions.explanation: Electron forward ⇒ Conventional current I is backward (towards back wall). Deflection force F is to the Right. Applying Fleming's left-hand rule: Middle finger (Current) pointing back, Thumb (Force) pointing right ⇒ Forefinger (Magnetic field) points vertically downwards.

questions.question: What is the direction of magnetic field lines OUTSIDE a bar magnet?
options: From North pole to South pole
From South pole to North pole
questions.answer: From North pole to South pole
questions.explanation: Outside the body of a bar magnet, magnetic field lines emerge from the North pole and curve around to enter the South pole.

questions.question: What is the direction of magnetic field lines INSIDE a bar magnet?
options: From North pole to South pole
From South pole to North pole
There are no field lines inside a magnet
questions.answer: From South pole to North pole
questions.explanation: Inside the magnet, field lines complete the continuous closed loop by travelling from the South pole back to the North pole.

questions.question: Why can two magnetic field lines NEVER intersect each other?
options: Because magnetic lines repel each other with electrostatic charge
Because at the point of intersection, a compass needle would point in two different directions simultaneously, which is impossible
Because they travel at the speed of sound
Because the magnetic field is a scalar quantity
questions.answer: Because at the point of intersection, a compass needle would point in two different directions simultaneously, which is impossible
questions.explanation: A unique point in a vector field can have only one resultant direction; intersection would imply two conflicting directions.

questions.question: Where is the magnetic field of a bar magnet the STRONGEST?
options: Near the magnetic poles where the field lines are most crowded
At the exact geometric centre of the magnet
questions.answer: Near the magnetic poles where the field lines are most crowded
questions.explanation: The density of field lines represents field intensity; lines are most densely packed near the magnetic poles.

questions.question: How can magnetic field lines around a bar magnet be made visually observable in a classroom laboratory?
options: By sprinkling fine iron filings on a smooth cardboard sheet tapped gently over the magnet
By shining green laser light through glass
By heating the magnet over a Bunsen flame
By placing the magnet in distilled water
questions.answer: By sprinkling fine iron filings on a smooth cardboard sheet tapped gently over the magnet
questions.explanation: Iron filings become magnetized by induction and align along magnetic field lines, creating visible patterns.

questions.question: What fundamental difference distinguishes magnetic field lines from electrostatic field lines?
options: Magnetic lines form continuous closed loops, whereas electrostatic lines begin on positive charges and end on negative charges
Magnetic lines can cross each other
Magnetic lines only exist in vacuum
questions.answer: Magnetic lines form continuous closed loops, whereas electrostatic lines begin on positive charges and end on negative charges
questions.explanation: Because magnetic monopoles do not exist, magnetic field lines are unbroken continuous loops.

title: Magnetic Field Due to a Straight Current-Carrying Conductor
tagline: Concentric circular field lines, dependence on current I (B ∝ I) and distance r (B ∝ 1/r).
theoryHtml:
1. Field Pattern Around a Straight Conductor

When a straight, vertical copper wire carrying electric current passes perpendicularly through a horizontal cardboard sprinkled with iron filings, gentle tapping causes the filings to align in a stunning pattern of concentric circles centered on the wire.

2. Characteristics of the Magnetic Field Pattern

  • The magnetic field lines are concentric circles lying in planes perpendicular to the straight conductor.
  • Near the wire, the concentric circles are closely spaced, indicating a strong magnetic field.
  • As the radial distance ($r$) from the wire increases, the circles become progressively wider and more spaced apart, indicating that field strength diminishes with distance.

3. Mathematical Proportionality of the Magnetic Field ($B$)

The magnitude of the magnetic field ($B$) at any point produced by a straight current-carrying wire depends on two physical factors:

  1. Directly proportional to the Current ($I$): $$B \propto I$$ Increasing the current flowing through the wire proportionally intensifies the magnetic field.
  2. Inversely proportional to the Distance ($r$): $$B \propto \frac{1}{r}$$ Moving twice as far away from the wire halves the magnetic field strength.

Combining both factors gives: $B \propto \frac{I}{r}$ (Biot-Savart Law / Ampère's Law: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$).
pointsToRemember: Magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying wire are concentric circles centered on the wire.
Field strength is directly proportional to current: $B \propto I$.
Field strength is inversely proportional to distance from the wire: $B \propto 1/r$.
keyNotes: If the current through a straight wire is tripled and the distance from the wire is doubled, the new magnetic field is $B' = \frac{3}{2} B = 1.5 B$.

questions.question: Why can NO two magnetic field lines ever intersect or cross each other?
options: They repel because they have identical mass
If they intersected, a compass needle placed at the point of intersection would have to point simultaneously in two different directions, which is physically impossible
They travel at the speed of light
Magnetic fields exist only in vacuum
questions.answer: If they intersected, a compass needle placed at the point of intersection would have to point simultaneously in two different directions, which is physically impossible
questions.explanation: At any point in space, the net magnetic field vector has a unique direction. Intersection would imply two resultant vectors, which is impossible.

questions.question: As the distance (r) from a straight current-carrying conductor INCREASES, the magnetic field strength (B):
questions.answer: Decreases inversely with distance (B ∝ 1/r)
questions.explanation: Magnetic field strength drops off inversely with radial distance from a straight wire (B ∝ 1/r).

questions.question: An electron enters a uniform magnetic field directed horizontally from left to right. If the electron is moving vertically downwards, what is the direction of the magnetic force acting on it?
options: Out of the page (towards the viewer)
questions.answer: Out of the page (towards the viewer)
questions.explanation: Electron downwards ⇒ conventional current is upwards. Field is rightwards. Applying Fleming's left-hand rule (Forefinger right, Middle finger up) gives Thumb pointing out of the page.

questions.question: A uniform magnetic field exists vertically downwards into the plane of the paper. A proton enters this field horizontally moving from left to right. What path will the proton follow?
options: It continues in a straight line with increasing speed
It deflects upwards towards the top of the page in a circular arc with constant speed
questions.answer: It deflects upwards towards the top of the page in a circular arc with constant speed
questions.explanation: Proton moving right ⇒ Current I = Right. Field B = Into paper. Middle finger Right, Forefinger Into paper ⇒ Thumb points upwards towards the top of page.

questions.question: What is the geometric pattern of magnetic field lines produced around a long straight current-carrying conductor?
options: Concentric circles centered on the wire in planes perpendicular to it
Straight parallel lines radiating outward like sunbeams
questions.answer: Concentric circles centered on the wire in planes perpendicular to it
questions.explanation: Field lines form closed concentric circles around the axis of the wire in planes perpendicular to the current.

questions.question: How does the magnitude of the magnetic field (B) produced by a straight current-carrying conductor change as the radial distance (r) from the wire INCREASES?
questions.answer: It decreases inversely (B ∝ 1/r)
questions.explanation: Magnetic field strength drops off inversely with perpendicular distance from the conductor (B ∝ 1/r).

questions.question: If the electric current flowing through a straight wire is TRIPLED, what happens to the magnetic field strength at a fixed distance from the wire?
questions.answer: It triples (3B)
questions.explanation: Because magnetic field strength is directly proportional to current (B ∝ I), tripling current triples field intensity.

questions.question: If the distance from a current-carrying straight wire is doubled, what happens to the magnetic field strength?
questions.answer: It is halved (B/2)
questions.explanation: Since B ∝ 1/r, doubling distance (r' = 2r) halves the magnetic field strength (B' = B/2).

questions.question: In which plane do the magnetic field lines of a vertical straight wire lie?
options: In horizontal planes perpendicular to the wire
In vertical planes parallel to the wire
Along the wire inside the copper
questions.answer: In horizontal planes perpendicular to the wire
questions.explanation: The concentric field circles lie entirely in planes perpendicular to the conductor's direction of current flow.

questions.question: Which of the following equations correctly represents the relationship between magnetic field B, current I, and distance r for a straight wire?
questions.answer: B ∝ I / r
questions.explanation: Magnetic field is directly proportional to current I and inversely proportional to distance r: B ∝ I/r.

title: Right-Hand Thumb Rule (Maxwell's Corkscrew Rule)
tagline: Determining circular field direction, curled fingers rule, and clockwise vs anticlockwise field.
theoryHtml:
1. The Right-Hand Thumb Rule

To determine the direction of the magnetic field lines produced by a current-carrying conductor, we use a simple and elegant mnemonic called the Right-Hand Thumb Rule:

"Imagine that you are grasping a current-carrying straight conductor in your RIGHT hand such that your outstretched thumb points in the direction of the electric current. Then, the direction in which your fingers curl naturally around the conductor gives the direction of the magnetic field lines."

2. Vertical Conductor Conventions

  • Current Flowing Vertically UPWARDS: Looking down from above, the curled fingers circle in an ANTI-CLOCKWISE (counter-clockwise) direction.
  • Current Flowing Vertically DOWNWARDS: Looking down from above, the curled fingers circle in a CLOCKWISE direction.

3. Maxwell's Corkscrew Rule

An alternative representation is Maxwell's Corkscrew Rule: If we consider a standard right-handed corkscrew being driven forward in the direction of current, the direction in which the handle of the corkscrew must be rotated gives the direction of the magnetic field lines.
pointsToRemember: Right-Hand Thumb Rule: Outstretched thumb indicates current; curled fingers indicate magnetic field direction.
Upward current $\rightarrow$ Anti-clockwise field lines (viewed from top).
Downward current $\rightarrow$ Clockwise field lines (viewed from top).
keyNotes: Always use your RIGHT hand! Grasping with your left hand will give the exact opposite (wrong) magnetic field direction.

questions.question: What does the degree of closeness (crowding) of magnetic field lines in a given region indicate?
options: The relative strength of the magnetic field (closer lines signify a stronger magnetic field)
The electric charge of the magnet
questions.answer: The relative strength of the magnetic field (closer lines signify a stronger magnetic field)
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux density (line crowding) directly represents magnetic field intensity; field lines are most crowded near the poles where the field is strongest.

questions.question: What is the pattern of magnetic field lines produced around a straight current-carrying metallic conductor?
options: Parallel straight lines along the wire
Concentric circles centred on the conductor in a plane perpendicular to the wire
questions.answer: Concentric circles centred on the conductor in a plane perpendicular to the wire
questions.explanation: Field lines around a straight current-carrying wire form coaxial concentric circles lying in perpendicular planes.

questions.question: A positively charged alpha particle projected towards the West is deflected towards the North by a magnetic field. What is the direction of the magnetic field?
options: Upwards (out of the plane / vertically upward)
questions.answer: Upwards (out of the plane / vertically upward)
questions.explanation: Positive charge West ⇒ Current I = West. Force F = North (Thumb). Middle finger = West, Thumb = North ⇒ Forefinger points vertically upwards.

questions.question: A circular wire loop is lying horizontally on a table. When viewed from above, electric current flows through the loop in a CLOCKWISE direction. What is the direction of the magnetic field at points INSIDE and OUTSIDE the loop?
options: Inside: Directed vertically downwards into the table; Outside: Directed vertically upwards out of the table
questions.answer: Inside: Directed vertically downwards into the table; Outside: Directed vertically upwards out of the table
questions.explanation: By Right-Hand Thumb Rule, curling right fingers clockwise forces the thumb to point downwards into the table inside the loop, and field lines loop back upwards outside the coil.

questions.question: Which rule is used to determine the DIRECTION of magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying wire?
questions.answer: Right-Hand Thumb Rule
questions.explanation: The Right-Hand Thumb Rule (or Maxwell's Corkscrew Rule) provides the circular magnetic field direction around a current.

questions.question: In a vertical straight conductor carrying electric current directed vertically UPWARDS, what is the direction of the magnetic field lines when viewed from above?
questions.answer: Anti-clockwise (counter-clockwise)
questions.explanation: With the right thumb pointing upwards, the fingers curl in an anti-clockwise direction when viewed from above.

questions.question: In a vertical wire carrying current directed vertically DOWNWARDS, what is the direction of the magnetic field lines when viewed from above?
questions.answer: Clockwise
questions.explanation: With the right thumb pointing downwards, the fingers curl in a clockwise direction when viewed from above.

questions.question: An electric current is flowing through a horizontal power line from East to West. What is the direction of the magnetic field at a point directly BELOW the wire?
questions.answer: Towards South
questions.explanation: Pointing the right thumb West, curled fingers underneath the wire point towards the South.

questions.question: What is the alternative physical rule that describes the same field direction as the Right-Hand Thumb Rule using a right-handed screw?
questions.answer: Maxwell's Corkscrew Rule
questions.explanation: Driving a right-handed corkscrew in the direction of current requires rotating it in the direction of the magnetic field.

questions.question: If an observer uses their LEFT hand instead of their right hand for the thumb rule, what error occurs?
options: The deduced direction of the magnetic field will be exactly reversed (180° wrong)
questions.answer: The deduced direction of the magnetic field will be exactly reversed (180° wrong)
questions.explanation: Using the left hand reverses the curl direction, giving the diametrically opposite direction.

title: Magnetic Field Due to a Current through a Circular Loop
tagline: Superposition of field lines, straight lines at the centre, and the Clock Face Rule.
theoryHtml:
1. Bending a Straight Conductor into a Circular Loop

Imagine bending a straight current-carrying wire into a circular loop. At every tiny segment of the circular wire, the magnetic field consists of concentric circles centered on that wire segment.

2. Evolution of Field Pattern towards the Centre

  • Near the circular wire rim, the magnetic field lines appear as tight concentric circles.
  • As we move inward towards the centre of the loop, the circles grow increasingly large.
  • At the exact centre of the circular loop, the arcs of these colossal circles become so vast that they appear as straight, parallel lines perpendicular to the plane of the coil.
  • Because current flows in opposite directions on opposite sides of the loop, the field contributions from every infinitesimal segment of the wire add up constructively in the same direction inside the loop.

3. Field Enhancement with Multiple Turns ($N$)

If a coil has $N$ circular turns wound closely together, the magnetic field produced is $N$ times as large as that produced by a single turn ($B \propto N \cdot I$). This occurs because the current in each turn has the same direction and their magnetic fields add together constructively.

4. The Clock Face Rule for Magnetic Polarity

Looking face-on at one side of a circular current-carrying coil:

  • If current flows in a CLOCKWISE direction $\rightarrow$ that face behaves as a SOUTH pole ($S$).
  • If current flows in an ANTI-CLOCKWISE direction $\rightarrow$ that face behaves as a NORTH pole ($N$).
pointsToRemember: Field lines at the centre of a circular current loop are uniform, straight, and perpendicular to the loop's plane.
A coil of $N$ turns produces a field $N$ times stronger than a single turn: $B \propto N \cdot I$.
Clock Face Rule: Clockwise current = South pole ($S$); Anti-clockwise current = North pole ($N$).
keyNotes: Every current-carrying circular loop acts as an ultra-thin magnetic dipole having a North face on one side and a South face on the opposite side.

questions.question: Which rule is used to find the direction of magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying conductor?
options: Right-Hand Thumb Rule (or Maxwell's Corkscrew Rule)
questions.answer: Right-Hand Thumb Rule (or Maxwell's Corkscrew Rule)
questions.explanation: Right-Hand Thumb Rule: Point right thumb in current direction; wrapped fingers show the direction of concentric magnetic field lines.

questions.question: If the electric current flowing through a straight vertical copper wire is DOUBLED, what happens to the magnetic field strength at a fixed distance from the wire?
questions.answer: It is doubled (B ∝ I)
questions.explanation: The magnetic field produced by a straight conductor is directly proportional to current (B ∝ I).

questions.question: Which of the following physical properties of a proton can change when it enters and moves freely in a magnetic field?
options: Velocity and momentum (direction of motion changes while speed remains constant)
questions.answer: Velocity and momentum (direction of motion changes while speed remains constant)
questions.explanation: Magnetic force is always perpendicular to velocity ($F perp v$), doing zero work. Kinetic energy and speed remain constant, but directional velocity and momentum change continuously.

questions.question: An electrical appliance of power 3.3 kW (3300 W) is operated on a 220 V line. Why is it dangerous to plug this appliance into a 5 A domestic socket?
options: The appliance will produce cold air
The appliance draws current I = 3300/220 = 15 A; drawing 15 A through a 5 A-rated socket causes severe resistive overheating of the wiring, melting insulation and creating a fire hazard
The appliance will reverse its rotation
The supply frequency will drop to 0 Hz
questions.answer: The appliance draws current I = 3300/220 = 15 A; drawing 15 A through a 5 A-rated socket causes severe resistive overheating of the wiring, melting insulation and creating a fire hazard
questions.explanation: Operating a 15 A load on a 5 A socket causes excessive I²R heating, risking electrical fire.

questions.question: What is the shape of the magnetic field lines at the EXACT CENTRE of a current-carrying circular loop?
options: Straight and parallel lines perpendicular to the plane of the coil
questions.answer: Straight and parallel lines perpendicular to the plane of the coil
questions.explanation: At the centre of the loop, the vast circular field arcs merge and appear as straight, parallel lines perpendicular to the loop plane.

questions.question: If a circular coil of wire has N turns wound closely together, how does its magnetic field compare to that of a single turn carrying the same current?
options: It is N times as strong
It is identical to a single turn
questions.answer: It is N times as strong
questions.explanation: Because current flows in the same direction in each turn, the magnetic fields of all N turns add up constructively: B ∝ N·I.

questions.question: According to the Clock Face Rule, if the current in a circular loop appears to flow in a CLOCKWISE direction to an observer, which magnetic pole does that face represent?
questions.answer: South pole (S)
questions.explanation: Clockwise current corresponds to a South magnetic pole (the letter S has arrows pointing clockwise at its ends).

questions.question: According to the Clock Face Rule, if the current in a circular loop appears to flow in an ANTI-CLOCKWISE direction, which magnetic pole does that face represent?
questions.answer: North pole (N)
questions.explanation: Anti-clockwise current corresponds to a North magnetic pole (the letter N has arrows pointing anti-clockwise at its tips).

questions.question: If a circular loop is lying horizontally on a tabletop and carrying an anti-clockwise current when viewed from above, what is the direction of the magnetic field at the centre of the loop?
options: Vertically upwards (pointing out of the table)
questions.answer: Vertically upwards (pointing out of the table)
questions.explanation: By the right-hand rule, curling fingers anti-clockwise causes the outstretched thumb to point vertically upwards out of the table.

questions.question: How does increasing the radius (R) of a circular loop carrying constant current affect the magnetic field strength at its centre?
options: Field strength decreases inversely with radius (B ∝ 1/R)
Field strength drops to zero instantly
questions.answer: Field strength decreases inversely with radius (B ∝ 1/R)
questions.explanation: At the centre of a circular loop, B = μ0 I / (2R); a larger radius places the wire segments farther from the centre, reducing field strength.

title: Magnetic Field in a Solenoid: Uniform Internal Field & Bar Magnet Equivalence
tagline: Helical coil, uniform parallel interior field lines, and equivalence to a bar magnet.
theoryHtml:
1. What is a Solenoid?

A solenoid is a long coil consisting of many closely wound turns of insulated copper wire wrapped in the shape of a cylinder.

2. The Magnetic Field Pattern of a Solenoid

When an electric current is passed through a solenoid, it produces a magnetic field pattern that is remarkably identical to that of a permanent bar magnet:

  • One end of the solenoid behaves as a magnetic North pole ($N$), while the opposite end behaves as a magnetic South pole ($S$).
  • Outside the solenoid, field lines emerge from the North pole and curve around to enter the South pole.
  • Inside the Solenoid: The magnetic field lines are parallel straight lines running along the longitudinal axis from South to North.

3. Uniformity of the Internal Field

Because the field lines inside the core of a solenoid are perfectly straight, equidistant, and parallel to each other, this proves that the magnetic field is completely UNIFORM (has the exact same magnitude and direction at every point inside the solenoid).

4. Factors Determining Internal Magnetic Field Strength ($B$)

$$B = \mu_0 \cdot n \cdot I$$
  • Directly proportional to the number of turns per unit length ($n = N/L$).
  • Directly proportional to the current magnitude ($I$).
  • Directly dependent on the core material inserted inside (permeability $\mu$).
pointsToRemember: A solenoid's magnetic field pattern is identical to that of a bar magnet.
Inside a solenoid, field lines are straight parallel lines, indicating a UNIFORM magnetic field.
Internal field strength depends on turns per unit length ($n$), current ($I$), and core material.
keyNotes: A uniform magnetic field is graphically represented by a set of equidistant, parallel straight lines with arrows pointing in the same direction.

questions.question: A long horizontal power line carries current from East to West. Viewed from the East end, what is the direction of the magnetic field lines around the wire?
questions.answer: Clockwise
questions.explanation: Applying the Right-Hand Thumb Rule with thumb pointing West (into the page from East), fingers curl in a clockwise direction.

questions.question: At the center of a circular current-carrying coil of wire, the magnetic field lines appear as:
options: Parallel straight lines perpendicular to the plane of the coil
questions.answer: Parallel straight lines perpendicular to the plane of the coil
questions.explanation: The curvature of concentric field loops from opposite sides of the circular loop cancels out, creating straight, uniform perpendicular field lines at the centre.

questions.question: In the human body, which two primary organs produce significant internal magnetic fields due to bio-electric nerve conduction?
questions.answer: Heart and brain
questions.explanation: Action potentials and ionic currents generate measurable biomagnetic fields in the heart (magnetocardiography) and brain (magnetoencephalography).

questions.question: A straight wire of length 0.2 m carries a current of 5 A at right angles to a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. What is the magnetic force acting on the wire?
What is the nature of the magnetic field inside a long current-carrying cylindrical solenoid?
options: Uniform (same magnitude and direction at all points, represented by parallel straight lines)
Increases as you move towards the ends
questions.answer: Uniform (same magnitude and direction at all points, represented by parallel straight lines)
questions.explanation: Field lines inside a solenoid are parallel and equidistant, demonstrating a completely uniform internal magnetic field.

questions.question: The magnetic field pattern produced by a current-carrying solenoid is virtually identical to that of which permanent magnet?
questions.answer: Bar magnet
questions.explanation: A solenoid acts as an artificial bar magnet, having a North pole at one end, South at the other, and identical external loops.

questions.question: What does a region of parallel, equidistant straight magnetic field lines indicate about the magnetic field?
options: The field is changing rapidly with time
questions.answer: The field is uniform
questions.explanation: Equidistant, parallel straight lines graphically represent a uniform vector field of constant magnitude and direction.

questions.question: How can the strength of the magnetic field inside a solenoid be substantially increased?
options: By inserting a soft iron rod inside the core and increasing the number of turns and current
By replacing copper wire with plastic wire
By dipping the solenoid in oil
By uncoiling the wire into a straight line
questions.answer: By inserting a soft iron rod inside the core and increasing the number of turns and current
questions.explanation: Field strength B = μ n I increases with higher turns per unit length (n), higher current (I), and high permeability core (soft iron).

questions.question: What is a solenoid?
options: A long cylindrical coil of many closely spaced turns of insulated copper wire
A permanent iron bar without wire
questions.answer: A long cylindrical coil of many closely spaced turns of insulated copper wire
questions.explanation: By definition, a solenoid is an insulated wire tightly wound into a helical cylindrical coil.

questions.question: If the direction of electric current in a solenoid is reversed, what happens to its magnetic poles?
options: The polarity reverses (the North pole becomes South, and South becomes North)
The field strength drops to zero
questions.answer: The polarity reverses (the North pole becomes South, and South becomes North)
questions.explanation: Reversing current reverses the circulatory curl direction, inverting the magnetic dipoles and swapping N and S poles.

title: Electromagnets: The Role of Soft Iron Core & Temporary Magnetization
tagline: High magnetic permeability, instantaneous magnetization, and zero retentivity.
theoryHtml:
1. What is an Electromagnet?

A strong magnetic field produced inside a current-carrying solenoid can be harnessed to magnetize a magnetic material placed inside the coil. A temporary magnet formed by placing a rod of soft iron inside a current-carrying solenoid is called an electromagnet.

2. Why Soft Iron is the Ideal Core Material

Soft iron is exclusively chosen as the core material for electromagnets because of two unique ferromagnetic properties:

  1. High Magnetic Permeability: Soft iron concentrates magnetic field lines immensely, multiplying the magnetic field strength of the solenoid by several thousand times.
  2. Low Retentivity (Zero Residual Magnetism): Soft iron is a temporary magnetic material. It magnetizes instantly when current is switched on, and loses all its magnetism immediately when current is switched off.

3. Controlling the Strength of an Electromagnet

Unlike permanent magnets whose strength is unalterable, an electromagnet's magnetic strength can be dynamically adjusted:

  • By increasing the electric current ($I$) using a rheostat.
  • By increasing the number of turns ($N$) in the solenoid coil.
  • By minimizing the air gap in its core geometry (e.g., U-shaped horseshoe electromagnets).
pointsToRemember: An electromagnet is a solenoid wrapped around a soft iron core.
Soft iron magnetizes easily and loses its magnetism completely when current is cut off (low retentivity).
Strength can be varied at will by altering current, turn count, or coil geometry.
keyNotes: Electromagnets are temporary magnets; switching off the electric switch immediately drops their magnetic attraction to zero, enabling scrap cranes to release heavy steel plates effortlessly.

questions.question: If a circular coil of wire has 'n' turns instead of a single turn, the magnetic field produced at its centre is:
options: n times larger (as the magnetic field of each individual turn adds up constructively in the same direction)
questions.answer: n times larger (as the magnetic field of each individual turn adds up constructively in the same direction)
questions.explanation: Since currents in all n turns circulate in the same direction, their magnetic fields superimpose linearly: B = n × B_single.

questions.question: A long cylindrical coil of many closely wrapped circular turns of insulated copper wire is called a:
questions.answer: Solenoid
questions.explanation: A solenoid consists of a helical coil of insulated copper wire wound in the shape of a cylinder.

questions.question: Which medical diagnostic imaging technique utilizes internal biomagnetic fields and external magnetic gradients to obtain high-resolution images of human organs?
questions.answer: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)
questions.explanation: MRI uses nuclear magnetic resonance of hydrogen protons in tissue water to generate diagnostic cross-sectional images.

questions.question: Two parallel wires carry steady currents in the SAME direction. What is the nature of the magnetic interaction between them?
options: They attract each other (Ampère's force law: parallel currents attract, anti-parallel currents repel)
questions.answer: They attract each other (Ampère's force law: parallel currents attract, anti-parallel currents repel)
questions.explanation: Parallel currents in the same direction generate attractive magnetic forces; opposing anti-parallel currents repel.

questions.question: What material is placed inside a solenoid to create a powerful TEMPORARY electromagnet?
questions.answer: Soft iron rod
questions.explanation: Soft iron has high permeability and low retentivity, magnetizing strongly under current and demagnetizing instantly when turned off.

questions.question: Why is soft iron described as having 'low retentivity'?
options: It retains all its magnetism forever
It loses virtually all its residual magnetism immediately when the magnetizing electric current is switched off
questions.answer: It loses virtually all its residual magnetism immediately when the magnetizing electric current is switched off
questions.explanation: Low retentivity means the material cannot retain residual magnetism once the external magnetic field ceases.

questions.question: Which of the following methods will INCREASE the magnetic strength of an electromagnet?
options: Decreasing the current flowing in the coil
Increasing the number of turns per unit length and increasing the current
Heating the core to red heat
questions.answer: Increasing the number of turns per unit length and increasing the current
questions.explanation: Field strength B ∝ n·I; increasing turns and current intensifies the magnetic field.

questions.question: Which of the following devices relies directly on an electromagnet for its operation?
questions.answer: Electric bell and relay switch
questions.explanation: Electric bells, relays, magnetic locks, and scrapyard lifting cranes utilize electromagnets that rapidly cycle on and off.

questions.question: What would happen if a scrap crane used a PERMANENT magnet instead of an electromagnet to lift junk cars?
options: The crane could not pick up the cars
The crane could lift the cars, but would be unable to release or drop them because the magnet cannot be switched off
The cars would turn into gold
questions.answer: The crane could lift the cars, but would be unable to release or drop them because the magnet cannot be switched off
questions.explanation: Permanent magnets cannot be de-energized; an electromagnet can drop loads instantly by opening the electrical switch.

questions.question: Can the polarity (North and South poles) of an electromagnet be reversed?
options: No, polarity is permanently fixed during manufacturing
Yes, simply by reversing the direction of electric current flowing through the solenoid coil
Only by striking it with a hammer
questions.answer: Yes, simply by reversing the direction of electric current flowing through the solenoid coil
questions.explanation: Inverting current flow reverses the magnetic field direction, instantly swapping the North and South poles.

title: Electromagnets vs Permanent Magnets: Core Materials & Applications
tagline: Soft iron vs Steel/Alnico, controllable vs fixed strength, and industrial applications.
theoryHtml:
1. Permanent Magnets: High Retentivity Materials

A permanent magnet is a magnet made of a ferromagnetic material that retains its magnetic properties for a prolonged duration without requiring an external electric current. Permanent magnets are manufactured from alloys having high retentivity and high coercivity:

  • Carbon Steel / Chromium Steel
  • Alnico: An alloy of Aluminium ($Al$), Nickel ($Ni$), and Cobalt ($Co$).
  • Neodymium (NdFeB): Modern rare-earth supermagnets.

2. Systematic Comparison

CharacteristicElectromagnet (Temporary)Permanent Magnet
Magnetism NatureTemporary; exists only while current flowsPermanent; persists indefinitely
Core MaterialSoft Iron (Low retentivity)Steel, Alnico, NdFeB (High retentivity)
Magnetic StrengthEasily varied by changing current or turnsFixed; cannot be varied easily
PolarityCan be reversed by reversing current directionFixed; North and South poles cannot be swapped
ApplicationsElectric bells, cranes, MRI scanners, relaysLoudspeakers, galvanometers, compasses
pointsToRemember: Electromagnets are temporary (soft iron core); Permanent magnets retain magnetism permanently (steel, alnico).
Electromagnet strength and polarity can be dynamically controlled; permanent magnet properties are fixed.
Alnico (Al-Ni-Co) and carbon steel are used to manufacture permanent magnets.
keyNotes: If steel is placed inside a solenoid, it magnetizes slowly but retains its magnetism permanently even after current is turned off, forming a permanent magnet.

questions.question: The magnetic field pattern produced by a current-carrying solenoid is virtually identical to that of a:
questions.answer: Bar magnet
questions.explanation: A current-carrying solenoid has dipole field lines emerging from one face (North pole) and re-entering the opposite face (South pole), mimicking a bar magnet.

questions.question: Which material is PERMANENTLY magnetized to make powerful permanent magnets (such as Alnico)?
options: Hard steel / Carbon steel / Alnico alloy
questions.answer: Hard steel / Carbon steel / Alnico alloy
questions.explanation: Hard ferromagnetic materials (steel, Alnico) possess high retentivity and coercivity, retaining permanent magnetism.

questions.question: What is the voltage and frequency of the domestic AC electric power supplied to households in India?
questions.answer: 220 V at 50 Hz
questions.explanation: Standard domestic single-phase alternating current supply in India is 220 V RMS at a frequency of 50 Hz.

questions.question: How does the magnetic field (B) at the centre of a circular loop change if its radius (r) is DOUBLED while keeping the current (I) constant?
questions.answer: It is halved (B ∝ 1/r)
questions.explanation: At the centre of a circular loop B = μ₀I / (2r); doubling radius r halves the magnetic field strength.

questions.question: Which of the following materials is PERMANENTLY magnetized to manufacture strong permanent magnets?
questions.answer: Alnico (Aluminium-Nickel-Cobalt alloy) or Carbon Steel
questions.explanation: Alnico and hardened carbon steel have high retentivity and coercivity, retaining strong magnetism permanently.

questions.question: What happens if a steel bar is placed inside a current-carrying solenoid for several minutes and the current is then switched off?
options: The steel loses all magnetism immediately
The steel retains its magnetism and becomes a permanent bar magnet
questions.answer: The steel retains its magnetism and becomes a permanent bar magnet
questions.explanation: Steel has high retentivity; once aligned by the solenoid field, its magnetic domains stay locked, forming a permanent magnet.

questions.question: What is a major operational advantage of an electromagnet over a permanent magnet?
options: Its magnetic strength can be varied by adjusting current, and its polarity can be reversed at will
It does not require any electric power
questions.answer: Its magnetic strength can be varied by adjusting current, and its polarity can be reversed at will
questions.explanation: Electromagnets offer complete dynamic control over on/off states, field strength, and polarity.

questions.question: Which of the following devices relies on a PERMANENT magnet rather than an electromagnet?
questions.answer: Magnetic compass needle and loudspeaker
questions.explanation: Compasses and audio speaker drivers rely on permanent magnets that maintain fixed, steady magnetic fields.

questions.question: What is the primary composition of the alloy 'Alnico'?
questions.answer: Aluminium, Nickel, and Cobalt
questions.explanation: Alnico is a ferromagnetic alloy composed predominantly of Aluminium (Al), Nickel (Ni), and Cobalt (Co).

questions.question: Why is soft iron NOT used to make permanent magnets?
options: Because its low retentivity causes it to lose its magnetism as soon as the external field is removed
Because it does not conduct electricity
questions.answer: Because its low retentivity causes it to lose its magnetism as soon as the external field is removed
questions.explanation: Soft iron easily loses its magnetic domain alignment, making it unsuitable for permanent magnets.

title: Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor in a Magnetic Field
tagline: Ampere's hypothesis of mutual force, Lorentz magnetic force (F = BIl sin θ), and maximum force condition.
theoryHtml:
1. André-Marie Ampère's Hypothesis (1820)

Following Oersted's discovery that a current-carrying wire exerts a mechanical deflecting force on a magnetic compass needle, French physicist André-Marie Ampère reasoned by Newton's third law of motion: If a current-carrying conductor exerts a force on a magnet, the magnet MUST exert an equal and opposite mechanical force on the current-carrying conductor!

2. The Kicking Wire Experiment

A flexible aluminium rod suspended horizontally between the poles of a strong U-shaped horseshoe magnet is connected in an electrical circuit:

  • When current is switched on, the aluminium rod is visibly thrust (kicked) sideways out of the magnetic gap.
  • Reversing the direction of current reverses the direction of the mechanical displacement.
  • Inverting the magnetic poles (swapping North and South) also reverses the displacement direction.

3. The Magnitude of the Magnetic Force ($F$)

The magnetic force ($F$) exerted on a conductor of length $l$ carrying current $I$ immersed in a uniform magnetic field $B$ is given by:

$$\mathbf{F = B \cdot I \cdot l \cdot \sin\theta}$$

Where $\theta$ is the angle between the conductor (current direction) and the magnetic field lines:

  • Maximum Force ($\theta = 90^\circ$): When the conductor is placed perpendicular to the magnetic field ($\sin 90^\circ = 1$): $$\mathbf{F_\text{max} = B \cdot I \cdot l}$$
  • Zero Force ($\theta = 0^\circ\text{ or }180^\circ$): When the conductor is placed parallel or anti-parallel to the magnetic field ($\sin 0^\circ = 0$): $$\mathbf{F = 0}$$
pointsToRemember: A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field experiences a mechanical deflecting force.
Force equation: $F = BIl\sin\theta$.
Maximum force occurs when conductor is PERPENDICULAR to the field ($\theta = 90^\circ$); ZERO force occurs when PARALLEL ($\theta = 0^\circ$).
keyNotes: If an electron or proton moves parallel to magnetic field lines, it experiences ZERO magnetic force ($F = 0$) and continues in a straight path with undeflected velocity.

questions.question: The magnetic field lines INSIDE a long current-carrying solenoid are in the form of parallel straight lines. This indicates that the magnetic field inside the solenoid is:
options: Uniform (same magnitude and direction at all interior points)
Maximum at the edges and zero inside
questions.answer: Uniform (same magnitude and direction at all interior points)
questions.explanation: Parallel equidistant field lines represent a spatially uniform magnetic field throughout the interior cavity of a long solenoid.

questions.question: An electromagnet consists of a core of __________ placed inside a current-carrying solenoid coil.
questions.answer: Soft iron
questions.explanation: Soft iron has high magnetic permeability and low retentivity; it strongly magnifies magnetic fields when energized and readily demagnetizes when current is switched off.

questions.question: When a current-carrying conductor is placed PARALLEL to the direction of a magnetic field (θ = 0° or 180°), what is the magnitude of the magnetic force acting on it?
questions.answer: Zero (F = 0)
questions.explanation: Since sin 0° = sin 180° = 0, no magnetic Lorentz force acts on a conductor aligned parallel to magnetic field lines.

questions.question: Which of the following precautions is ESSENTIAL to prevent electrical overloading in domestic household circuits?
options: Connecting multiple high-power heaters to a single multi-plug extension cord
Distributing high-wattage appliances across separate 15 A circuits, avoiding multiple loads on single sockets, and installing appropriately rated fuses/MCBs
Replacing copper wires with thin iron wires
questions.answer: Distributing high-wattage appliances across separate 15 A circuits, avoiding multiple loads on single sockets, and installing appropriately rated fuses/MCBs
questions.explanation: Proper circuit segmentation and fuse protection prevent current overload.

questions.question: Under what condition is the mechanical force experienced by a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field MAXIMUM?
options: When the conductor is parallel to the magnetic field (θ = 0°)
When the conductor is perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field (θ = 90°)
When the conductor is placed at 45°
questions.answer: When the conductor is perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field (θ = 90°)
questions.explanation: Since F = BIl sin θ, maximum force occurs when sin θ = 1, which corresponds to θ = 90° (perpendicular alignment).

questions.question: What is the force on a current-carrying wire placed PARALLEL to the direction of a uniform magnetic field?
questions.answer: Zero (F = 0)
questions.explanation: When parallel, θ = 0°, so sin 0° = 0, which yields F = BIl sin 0° = 0.

questions.question: A positively charged alpha particle projected towards the West is deflected towards the North by a magnetic field. What is the direction of the magnetic field?
questions.answer: Upward out of the plane
questions.explanation: Applying Fleming's left-hand rule: Forefinger (Field) = Upward, Centre finger (Current West) = West, Thumb (Force North) = North.

questions.question: Who first hypothesized that a magnet must exert an equal and opposite mechanical force on a current-carrying wire?
questions.answer: André-Marie Ampère
questions.explanation: Ampère reasoned from Newton's third law that if current deflects a magnet, the magnet must exert a reciprocal force on the conductor.

questions.question: If an electron enters a uniform magnetic field directed from left to right along a path that is PARALLEL to the field lines, what happens to its trajectory?
options: It experiences zero force and continues to travel straight in its original direction
It stops dead in its tracks
questions.answer: It experiences zero force and continues to travel straight in its original direction
questions.explanation: Because θ = 0°, magnetic Lorentz force F = qvB sin 0° = 0, so the electron continues undeflected in a straight line.

questions.question: Which of the following factors does NOT determine the magnitude of the force on a straight conductor in a magnetic field?
options: Color of the wire's plastic insulation
Length of conductor l inside the field
questions.answer: Color of the wire's plastic insulation
questions.explanation: Force depends solely on B, I, l, and angle θ (F = BIl sin θ); insulation color has zero physical effect.

title: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: The Motor Rule (Thrust, Field, Current)
tagline: Three mutually perpendicular fingers: Thumb = Force/Motion, Forefinger = Field, Centre finger = Current.
theoryHtml:
1. Fleming's Left-Hand Rule (The Motor Rule)

To determine the direction of the mechanical force (thrust) exerted on a current-carrying conductor placed inside an external magnetic field, John Ambrose Fleming formulated Fleming's Left-Hand Rule:

"Stretch the thumb, forefinger, and centre (middle) finger of your LEFT hand mutually perpendicular to each other. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the centre finger in the direction of electric current, then the thumb will point in the direction of motion or the mechanical force (thrust) acting on the conductor."

2. The FBI Mnemonic

An easy way to remember the mapping of the three perpendicular fingers of the LEFT hand:

  • Thumb ($\mathbf{F}$): Force / Thrust / Motion ($\mathbf{F}\text{BI}$)
  • Forefinger ($\mathbf{B}$): Magnetic Field ($\text{F}\mathbf{B}\text{I}$)
  • Centre Finger ($\mathbf{I}$): Electric Current ($\text{FB}\mathbf{I}$)

3. Primary Applications of Fleming's Left-Hand Rule

This rule governs all electromagnetic devices where electrical energy is converted into mechanical motion:

  • Electric Motors (ceiling fans, washing machines, electric vehicles)
  • Moving-Coil Loudspeakers (converts electrical audio signals into cone vibration)
  • Galvanometers & Ammeters (pointer deflection against a spring)
pointsToRemember: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule is the 'Motor Rule': converts electrical current into mechanical motion.
FBI Mnemonic: Thumb = Force ($F$), Forefinger = Field ($B$), Centre finger = Current ($I$).
All three fingers must be held mutually perpendicular ($90^\circ$ to each other).
keyNotes: For moving charged particles: the direction of current ($I$) is along the motion of positive charges (protons/alpha particles), but OPPOSITE to the motion of negative charges (electrons)!

questions.question: Which French scientist suggested that since a current-carrying conductor exerts a magnetic force on a magnet, a magnet must also exert an equal and opposite force on the conductor?
questions.answer: André-Marie Ampère
questions.explanation: André-Marie Ampère applied Newton's third law to electromagnetism, proposing reciprocal mechanical forces between magnets and conductors.

questions.question: When is the mechanical force experienced by a current-carrying conductor placed in an external magnetic field MAXIMUM?
options: When the conductor is parallel to the magnetic field (θ = 0°)
When the conductor is perpendicular to the magnetic field (θ = 90°)
questions.answer: When the conductor is perpendicular to the magnetic field (θ = 90°)
questions.explanation: Force F = I L B sin θ; maximum force (F_max = ILB) occurs when θ = 90° (current perpendicular to magnetic field).

questions.question: In a standard domestic 3-wire electrical supply cable, what are the standard insulation colours for the Live, Neutral, and Earth wires in India?
options: Live: Black; Neutral: Red; Earth: Green
Live: Red; Neutral: Black; Earth: Green
Live: Green; Neutral: Red; Earth: Black
Live: White; Neutral: Blue; Earth: Yellow
questions.answer: Live: Red; Neutral: Black; Earth: Green
questions.explanation: Traditional colour codes in Indian domestic wiring: Live = Red (or brown), Neutral = Black (or blue), Earth = Green (or green/yellow).

questions.question: A compass needle is placed near a vertical current-carrying wire. If the current in the wire flows downwards (from ceiling to floor), in what direction does the North pole of the compass needle deflect when placed to the EAST of the wire?
questions.answer: Towards the South
questions.explanation: Current downwards ⇒ right hand thumb points down. Looking from above, field lines circulate CLOCKWISE. At the East position, the tangent to a clockwise circle points SOUTH.

questions.question: In Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, which finger represents the direction of the MAGNETIC FIELD?
questions.answer: Forefinger (Index finger)
questions.explanation: By Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, the forefinger represents the direction of the magnetic field (B).

questions.question: In Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, which finger represents the direction of the MECHANICAL FORCE (thrust)?
questions.answer: Thumb
questions.explanation: The outstretched thumb represents the direction of mechanical force or motion (F).

questions.question: In Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, which finger represents the direction of ELECTRIC CURRENT?
questions.answer: Centre (Middle) finger
questions.explanation: The centre (middle) finger represents the direction of electric current (I).

questions.question: A beam of electrons moving horizontally towards the right enters a magnetic field directed vertically downwards. In which direction is the electron beam deflected?
questions.answer: Into the page (away from observer)
questions.explanation: Electrons move right, so conventional current is LEFT. Field is DOWN. By Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: Forefinger DOWN, Centre finger LEFT => Thumb points INTO the page.

questions.question: Which of the following devices operates on the principle described by Fleming's Left-Hand Rule?
questions.answer: Electric motor
questions.explanation: An electric motor converts electrical current in a magnetic field into mechanical motion via Fleming's Left-Hand Rule.

questions.question: What is the angle between any two adjacent fingers in Fleming's Left-Hand Rule?
questions.answer: 90° (mutually perpendicular)
questions.explanation: The thumb, forefinger, and centre finger are held mutually perpendicular to each other (90°).
